Analyze vulnerability results and manage the remediation process. Establish vulnerability performance indicators and develop reports. Collaborate with other infrastructure team members with identity management and multi-factor authentication. Network and Security Design Development Participates in network and security design, configuration, and testing activities for both corporate and customer facing network infrastructure. Investigates, tests, recommends, and implements. Related duties as assigned. Network related certifications (e.g., CCNA, CCNP, CCIE, PCNSE) preferred. The ability to move and transport equipment weighing up to 50 lbs. Frequent standing, walking, bending, and reaching during equipment installation or servicing. Travel to Lumos locations as needed, including occasional overnight stays. Work in office, field, and construction site environments in various weather conditions. Continuous use of vision, hearing, speech, and reasoning to perform job duties. Benefits & Perks Our commitment to communities includes recruiting and rewarding the Lumos team members who are working together to build a brighter tomorrow. We Have Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage. Competitive compensation packages, including bonus options for eligible positions. Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays. Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs). 100% employer-paid life and disability insurance. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with access to professional support for life’s challenges. 401K plan w/ up to 5% employer contribution and a self-directed brokerage option. Wellness program offering education and cash incentives for gym attendance and nutrition programs. Employee referral bonuses. Discounts on Lumos Fiber Internet for employees who live in our service areas. Applicant Eligibility Notice Applicants must be at least eighteen (18) years of age at the time of application. We have a longstanding policy of providing a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of each individual and is free from all forms of employment discrimination, including harassment, because of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. review_candidates.title: Performance Engineer - Open Source
review_candidates.description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1000+ colleagues in 70+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder led, profitable and growing. We have created a new career path at Canonical for Performance Engineers who bring exceptional clarity to software performance, correctness and efficiency. We are adding these roles to every engineering team at the company. As an open source platform, we have teams that work at every level of the software stack - from the kernel up through server and desktop applications, all the way to the web. We are adding roles with this focus in every engineering team in the company, to act as drivers of performance engineering skills, tools, culture and insights to our entire product range . We have also created a central performance engineering team, where we will drive shared tools, dashboarding capabilities, measurement frameworks, analytical capabilities and skills. We call this career focus ' percorr ' because we have found that the same deep insights that enable sophisticated performance measurement and design also enable teams to improve their harnesses and frameworks for correctness. Understanding not only the application, but the runtime, the compiler, and the system, all the way down to the CPU, gives an engineer the ability to think creatively and with insight about the right things to measure, and the right ways to verify correctness. We have found that performance engineers will often improve the deepest and trickiest areas of our test harnesses, and unblock their teams to test and measure previously 'dark' aspects of their work. We also have teams that work with every major silicon vendor and cloud, with a particular emphasis on performance optimisation of the entire stack for that architecture, CPU family or hypervisor. Our goal is to ensure that Ubuntu users can select whatever platform they want for their workloads and know they have access to the very best performance and efficiency across the entire stack from kernel to codec. review_candidates.title: Enterprise Architect – Digital & Commerce Transformation
review_candidates.description: About The Role GES needs an eCommerce Architect who can bring order, speed, and architectural discipline to a high-visibility global transformation already in motion. The GES Store program spans commerce, content, integrations, payments, tax, reporting, regional rollout, vendor execution, and operational stabilization. The priority is not more analysis. The priority is better decisions, clearer ownership, and architecture that can scale. This role is expected to lead from the front. The Architect will challenge assumptions, expose weak designs, force tradeoffs into the open, and drive decisions to closure. This is not a system implementation role and it is not passive advisory. It requires a senior leader who can work through ambiguity, make practical calls, and align business, IT, PMO, engineering, vendors, and platform partners around one executable architecture. The Architect owns architecture governance and decision quality. That means approving or rejecting designs, escalating unresolved tradeoffs, clarifying ownership, and preventing short-term delivery pressure from creating long-term platform debt. The right candidate will be comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, documenting the rationale, and holding teams accountable for the path forward. This role will eventually transform into an overall Enterprise Architect for the entire GES IT landscape heading the Architecture Review Board (ARB). Program Scope (Indicative) Replace and modernize legacy commerce capabilities with a scalable global eCommerce platform. Support multi-region rollout across the United States, Canada, UK, EMEA, and future markets. Enterprise integrations across ERP, CRM, payments, tax, reporting, search, content, identity, and operational systems. Stabilize live capabilities while addressing root architectural issues and technical debt. Architectural remediation across commerce, front-end, content, data, integration, and support models. Governance across internal technology teams, business stakeholders, implementation vendors, platform partners, and PMO leadership. What Good Looks Like Ambiguity is reduced fast. Decisions are framed, owned, made, and documented. Architecture ownership is explicit across platforms, integrations, data, vendors, and workstreams. Decision velocity improves without bypassing governance or hiding risk. Business, IT, PMO, and vendors operate from one target architecture and one set of rules. Delivery teams execute against practical designs that scale beyond the first release. Key Responsibilities Decision Authority (Empowered To) Approve, reject, or send back architecture designs, integration patterns, data flows, platform configuration choices, and technical guardrails. Stop or escalate work that conflicts with the approved architecture, creates avoidable debt, or introduces unmanaged risk. Force decision clarity when teams are working from conflicting assumptions. Escalate unresolved tradeoffs to IT and Business sponsors with options, recommendation, impact, and required decision date. Challenge designs, sequencing, estimates, and delivery assumptions when they do not support the program outcome. Architecture & Strategy Own the end-to-end platform architecture across commerce, front end, content, integrations, identity, payments, tax, reporting, and operational support. Define the target-state architecture and the roadmap to move from current constraints to scalable global capability. Identify architectural gaps, root causes, dependencies, and remediation priorities. Convert technical tradeoffs into sponsor-level decisions with clear consequences. Protect long-term platform health while keeping near-term delivery moving. Integration & Data Architecture Define standard integration patterns across ERP, CRM, commerce, payments, tax, content, reporting, and internal operational systems. Replace brittle point-to-point thinking with reusable, governed integration patterns where they make sense. Clarify data ownership, system of record, synchronization rules, failure handling, retry logic, and reconciliation expectations. Ensure integration designs are scalable, observable, secure, and supportable across regions. Align data, integration, application, and infrastructure teams around designs that can actually be built and supported. Architecture Governance & Standards Stand up and run the program Architecture Review Board with enough structure to control risk and enough speed to support delivery. Define the required standards, artifacts, decision logs, review cadence, and approval criteria. Maintain architecture decision records that document options considered, recommendation, approval, rationale, and downstream impact. Use governance to enable delivery, not create process drag. Surface tradeoffs early, prevent rework, and keep workstreams aligned to the approved direction. Vendor & Partner Alignment Ensure vendors, platform partners, and internal teams design against one architecture, not competing versions of the truth. Challenge vendor designs that are not scalable, supportable, or aligned to the target state. Hold partners accountable for technical outcomes, not activity, staffing, or deliverable volume. Resolve cross-vendor design conflicts before they become delivery blockers. Escalate commercial, ownership, or accountability issues when they block architecture decisions. Delivery Alignment Ensure architecture shows up in the build, test, release, and support model. Work with PMO, engineering, QA, integration, infrastructure, business, and vendors to turn architecture into executable plans. Identify architectural dependencies, sequencing constraints, and decision points that affect delivery milestones. Support issue triage and root cause analysis where defects, instability, or rework indicate deeper architectural problems. Give teams clear direction so they move faster with fewer assumptions, fewer debates, and less rework. Execution Expectations Make decisions fast enough for an in-flight transformation and disciplined enough to control risk. Bring clarity when teams are stuck in debate, unclear ownership, or competing assumptions. Enable delivery with usable direction, not abstract architecture theory. Favor practical, scalable solutions over over-engineered designs that slow the program down. Escalate early when a decision requires sponsor alignment, funding impact, scope tradeoff, or cross-workstream prioritization. Document decisions so teams can execute without reopening the same debate. Required Qualifications Senior architecture leadership experience on enterprise digital, commerce, platform, or integration transformation programs. Proven ability to shape eCommerce ecosystems across commerce platform, front end, content, payments, tax, order flow, reporting, and downstream operations. Strong integration architecture experience across ERP, CRM, middleware, APIs, events, batch processing, data synchronization, and exception handling. Experience establishing architecture governance, decision logs, standards, and design review discipline in complex delivery environments. Experience operating in multi-vendor, multi-workstream programs where ownership and design authority must be actively enforced. Ability to communicate architecture decisions clearly to executives, sponsors, PMO, engineers, vendors, and operational leaders. Preferred Qualifications Experience with BigCommerce or similar enterprise commerce platforms such as Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Adobe Commerce, CommerceTools, Shopify Plus, or SAP Commerce. Experience with B2B commerce, account structures, price lists, catalogs, promotions, customer groups, checkout complexity, and operational workflows. Experience supporting multi-region or global commerce rollouts with localization, currency, tax, language, payments, and regional operating differences. Experience with headless or composable commerce ecosystems, including front-end frameworks, CMS, search, personalization, and content operations. Experience with Azure-based integration patterns, API management, serverless orchestration, monitoring, and DevOps-enabled delivery. Critical Traits Strong point of view: Brings recommendations and the rationale behind them. Comfortable saying no: Stops weak designs, risky shortcuts, and decisions that create avoidable debt. Executive presence: Explains architecture choices in business terms and drives sponsor-level decisions. Operates in ambiguity: Moves the work forward without perfect information or full consensus. Accountability mindset: Owns architectural outcomes through implementation, not just design approval. Pragmatic judgment: Knows when to standardize, when to compromise, and when to escalate. Work Environment Our team members are our family, so we help our team members care for their families. The rewards of joining GES are extensive. We offer a comprehensive benefits package to all full-time employees. Here are some of the highlights: Competitive salaries 401K with company match Healthcare/vision/dental insurance Wellness benefits Career development program Employee assistance program Vacation time Community involvement opportunities Team activities And much more……

review_candidates.title: Senior Scheduler, Corporate
review_candidates.description: NexGen is seeking a Senior Scheduler to join the team! This position will require 50% travel. Responsibilities Why NexGen? NexGen Contracting, the self-perform arm of Gray, is based in Franklin, TN, and specializes in executing turnkey project scopes, including concrete, steel, millwright, and finishes. NexGen is fully integrated with Gray Construction and serves as a preferred subcontractor. The NexGen team is made of career, trade-specific professionals and core craftsmen with decades of experience who are dedicated to meeting our customers’ unique needs. NexGen offers a wide range of self-perform services, which include supervision, administration, craft labor, materials, tools, documentation, consumables, and safety devices to successfully carry projects from start to finish. Why Gray? Gray is a fully integrated, global service provider deeply rooted in engineering, design, and construction, along with smart manufacturing and equipment manufacturing services. Consistently ranked as a leader in the industry, we focus on the following markets for domestic and international customers: Food & Beverage, Manufacturing, Automotive, Distribution, Mission Critical, and Commercial. Founded in 1960, Gray’s robust offering enables us to create one-of-a-kind solutions at the highest levels of customization, delivering unmatched precision and partnership to some of the world’s most sophisticated organizations. Still, these areas don’t define Gray—our people do. Passion, commitment, and a great team spirit all speak to the team members at Gray. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Business or related discipline. Minimum seven (7) years of construction scheduling experience. Leading scheduling efforts on large/and or multiple projects Must be technically capable and experienced in the use of the most recent version(s) of Microsoft Project and Primavera (P6). Excellent oral and written communication skills. Demonstrate a positive attitude and excellence in customer service. Detail oriented with effective organization and coordination skills. Experience working in a team environment. Computer knowledge and efficiency, including Microsoft Office products. The new team member should be an energetic, self-motivated individual who enjoys a team environment, as well as a passion for collaboration and professional development. If you are a high achiever striving to exceed expectations in a fast-paced innovative company, then Gray is the place for you. The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. What We Expect… (Essential Functions) Oversee scheduling activities across all divisions and active projects-building out the scheduling Department for NexGen Contracting Develop, manage, and maintain integrated master project schedules that establish engineering, procurement, fabrication, material delivery, commissioning, and construction sequences in accordance with contract requirements and project objectives. Lead schedule development efforts during project planning and execution phases, collaborating with engineering, procurement, construction, subcontractors, vendors, and client stakeholders to ensure alignment with project milestones and deliverables. Facilitate periodic schedule reviews and updates with project teams, subcontractors, equipment suppliers, and client representatives to ensure schedule accuracy and timely identification of potential impacts. Analyze and validate logical relationships, critical path activities, schedule constraints, and resource requirements across complex industrial construction projects. Serve as the project scheduling subject matter expert, providing guidance and recommendations to project leadership regarding schedule strategy, recovery planning, risk mitigation, and performance improvement opportunities. Utilize advanced scheduling software, including Primavera P6 and Microsoft Project, to develop, maintain, and analyze cost-loaded and resource-loaded schedules. Lead implementation and analysis of Earned Value Management (EVM) systems, integrating schedule and cost performance data to measure project progress and forecast outcomes. Prepare and present executive-level schedule reports, dashboards, progress analyses, critical path assessments, and forecast completion scenarios to project management, clients, and senior leadership. Perform schedule risk assessments, what-if analyses, and scenario planning to identify potential schedule impacts and recommend mitigation and recovery strategies. Support contract administration efforts through schedule analysis, delay evaluations, time impact analyses, extension-of-time requests, and claims documentation when required. Establish and maintain project scheduling standards, procedures, and best practices across multiple projects and project teams. Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior schedulers and project controls personnel, supporting their professional development and ensuring consistency in scheduling practices. Monitor project performance trends and proactively identify positive and negative impacts to project execution, communicating findings and recommendations to project leadership. Conduct regular field visits to validate progress, verify installed quantities, assess productivity trends, and ensure schedule updates accurately reflect site conditions. Develop and present visual planning tools, including look-ahead schedules, schedule simulations, progress curves, dashboards, and sequencing presentations to support project execution and stakeholder communication. Produce detailed schedule analyses, variance reports, forecasting models, and impact assessments to support informed project decision-making. Interface professionally with clients, contractors, subcontractors, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders while representing the best interests of the organization. Support portfolio-level reporting and provide schedule oversight for multiple projects when required, ensuring consistency, accuracy, and adherence to organizational project controls standards. Promote and maintain safe work practices while performing field assessments and project site reviews. Other duties as assigned. Visa Sponsorship: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Physical Demands & Work Environment The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this position, the team member is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands, reach with hands or arms and talk or hear. They may occasionally be required to climb or balance, stoop, kneel, or crouch. Must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required include close vision. Generally, normal office environment where noise level is moderate and temperature/humidity is controlled. Overtime may be required. Supervisory Responsibilities This position may have supervisory responsibilities. EEO Disclaimer Gray is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer and welcomes everyone to apply. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

review_candidates.description: Who We Are Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact. To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive. What You'll Do You will join our Public Sector Economic Affairs team with a specific focus on Infrastructure, Transport, and City Development (P-ITC), helping to activate our work in construction and infrastructure project delivery. Key topics include financing, funding & PPPs, cost optimization, capital project excellence, and adaptation & resilience in Public Infrastructure. As a Senior Analyst on the Client Focus path within BCG's Public Sector Practice Area, you will deliver Impact Across Three Core Areas Client Delivery: Work as part of a global team on active client engagements, applying subject matter expertise and BCG Vantage assets including tools, frameworks, data, and workshops to drive strong outcomes. Occasional on-site travel is expected during staffing assignments. Business Development: Partner with business leaders to shape and win new work, contributing to proposals and client workshops with differentiated and sector specific perspectives and market insights. Knowledge & Capability Building: Develop intellectual property and assets for the topic area, and support the onboarding and training of junior colleagues. We partner with a diverse set of public and private stakeholders including federal, state, and local government agencies, transportation authorities, transit operators, municipalities, and engineering and construction firms to plan, deliver, and optimize large-scale infrastructure systems across the full project lifecycle. Our work spans roads and airports, rail and transit, ports and logistics, and cities and urban development, with the ultimate goal of helping partners build infrastructure that connects communities, drives economic opportunity, and creates a more sustainable future. YOU'RE GOOD AT Solving client problems through formulating relevant research and/or analytical approaches within the infrastructure sector context, including but not limited to: Infrastructure development (incl. Energy Assets, Defense infra & Data Centers) Water / Irrigation Waste management Cost, quality, and time optimization across infra. construction project lifecycle Communicating with case teams and clients team members, in a credible and confident way Working collaboratively and effectively in a group dynamic often virtual, proficient in agile ways of working Being flexible and bringing a curious and creative mindset, open to new things and able to propose innovative ideas Navigating complexity and ambiguity What You'll Bring Hands-on experience working with or on several large, capital Intensive, Infrastructure construction projects 2+ years of consulting experience in relevant infrastructure project delivery required; candidates with consulting experience strongly preferred. In lieu of consulting experience, 3+ years minimum industry experience required; 4-6+ years of industry experience strongly preferred Bachelor's Degree required (advanced degree preferred) Fluency in English U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. federal government security clearance Strong business acumen and problem-solving capabilities Strong written and verbal communication skills Familiarity with government systems and processes, with comfort navigating public sector environments Confident engaging external stakeholders independently, from procurement teams to client contacts Who You'll Work With As a Senior Analyst – BCG Vantage on our Client Focus path, you will work face to face with clients and with BCG Project Leaders, Associates and Consultants. In the period between cases, you will collaborate with global topic leads and colleagues across BCG to bring expertise and capabilities to the service of our internal and external clients. Our team is made up a diverse pool of BCG Vantage positions that allow us to pursue exciting, innovative BCG Vantage careers. Additional info In the US, we have a compensation transparency approach. new_matches.title: Enterprise Architect – Digital & Commerce Transformation
new_matches.description: About The Role GES needs an eCommerce Architect who can bring order, speed, and architectural discipline to a high-visibility global transformation already in motion. The GES Store program spans commerce, content, integrations, payments, tax, reporting, regional rollout, vendor execution, and operational stabilization. The priority is not more analysis. The priority is better decisions, clearer ownership, and architecture that can scale. This role is expected to lead from the front. The Architect will challenge assumptions, expose weak designs, force tradeoffs into the open, and drive decisions to closure. This is not a system implementation role and it is not passive advisory. It requires a senior leader who can work through ambiguity, make practical calls, and align business, IT, PMO, engineering, vendors, and platform partners around one executable architecture. The Architect owns architecture governance and decision quality. That means approving or rejecting designs, escalating unresolved tradeoffs, clarifying ownership, and preventing short-term delivery pressure from creating long-term platform debt. The right candidate will be comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, documenting the rationale, and holding teams accountable for the path forward. This role will eventually transform into an overall Enterprise Architect for the entire GES IT landscape heading the Architecture Review Board (ARB). Program Scope (Indicative) Replace and modernize legacy commerce capabilities with a scalable global eCommerce platform. Support multi-region rollout across the United States, Canada, UK, EMEA, and future markets. Enterprise integrations across ERP, CRM, payments, tax, reporting, search, content, identity, and operational systems. Stabilize live capabilities while addressing root architectural issues and technical debt. Architectural remediation across commerce, front-end, content, data, integration, and support models. Governance across internal technology teams, business stakeholders, implementation vendors, platform partners, and PMO leadership. What Good Looks Like Ambiguity is reduced fast. Decisions are framed, owned, made, and documented. Architecture ownership is explicit across platforms, integrations, data, vendors, and workstreams. Decision velocity improves without bypassing governance or hiding risk. Business, IT, PMO, and vendors operate from one target architecture and one set of rules. Delivery teams execute against practical designs that scale beyond the first release. Key Responsibilities Decision Authority (Empowered To) Approve, reject, or send back architecture designs, integration patterns, data flows, platform configuration choices, and technical guardrails. Stop or escalate work that conflicts with the approved architecture, creates avoidable debt, or introduces unmanaged risk. Force decision clarity when teams are working from conflicting assumptions. Escalate unresolved tradeoffs to IT and Business sponsors with options, recommendation, impact, and required decision date. Challenge designs, sequencing, estimates, and delivery assumptions when they do not support the program outcome. Architecture & Strategy Own the end-to-end platform architecture across commerce, front end, content, integrations, identity, payments, tax, reporting, and operational support. Define the target-state architecture and the roadmap to move from current constraints to scalable global capability. Identify architectural gaps, root causes, dependencies, and remediation priorities. Convert technical tradeoffs into sponsor-level decisions with clear consequences. Protect long-term platform health while keeping near-term delivery moving. Integration & Data Architecture Define standard integration patterns across ERP, CRM, commerce, payments, tax, content, reporting, and internal operational systems. Replace brittle point-to-point thinking with reusable, governed integration patterns where they make sense. Clarify data ownership, system of record, synchronization rules, failure handling, retry logic, and reconciliation expectations. Ensure integration designs are scalable, observable, secure, and supportable across regions. Align data, integration, application, and infrastructure teams around designs that can actually be built and supported. Architecture Governance & Standards Stand up and run the program Architecture Review Board with enough structure to control risk and enough speed to support delivery. Define the required standards, artifacts, decision logs, review cadence, and approval criteria. Maintain architecture decision records that document options considered, recommendation, approval, rationale, and downstream impact. Use governance to enable delivery, not create process drag. Surface tradeoffs early, prevent rework, and keep workstreams aligned to the approved direction. Vendor & Partner Alignment Ensure vendors, platform partners, and internal teams design against one architecture, not competing versions of the truth. Challenge vendor designs that are not scalable, supportable, or aligned to the target state. Hold partners accountable for technical outcomes, not activity, staffing, or deliverable volume. Resolve cross-vendor design conflicts before they become delivery blockers. Escalate commercial, ownership, or accountability issues when they block architecture decisions. Delivery Alignment Ensure architecture shows up in the build, test, release, and support model. Work with PMO, engineering, QA, integration, infrastructure, business, and vendors to turn architecture into executable plans. Identify architectural dependencies, sequencing constraints, and decision points that affect delivery milestones. Support issue triage and root cause analysis where defects, instability, or rework indicate deeper architectural problems. Give teams clear direction so they move faster with fewer assumptions, fewer debates, and less rework. Execution Expectations Make decisions fast enough for an in-flight transformation and disciplined enough to control risk. Bring clarity when teams are stuck in debate, unclear ownership, or competing assumptions. Enable delivery with usable direction, not abstract architecture theory. Favor practical, scalable solutions over over-engineered designs that slow the program down. Escalate early when a decision requires sponsor alignment, funding impact, scope tradeoff, or cross-workstream prioritization. Document decisions so teams can execute without reopening the same debate. Required Qualifications Senior architecture leadership experience on enterprise digital, commerce, platform, or integration transformation programs. Proven ability to shape eCommerce ecosystems across commerce platform, front end, content, payments, tax, order flow, reporting, and downstream operations. Strong integration architecture experience across ERP, CRM, middleware, APIs, events, batch processing, data synchronization, and exception handling. Experience establishing architecture governance, decision logs, standards, and design review discipline in complex delivery environments. Experience operating in multi-vendor, multi-workstream programs where ownership and design authority must be actively enforced. Ability to communicate architecture decisions clearly to executives, sponsors, PMO, engineers, vendors, and operational leaders. Preferred Qualifications Experience with BigCommerce or similar enterprise commerce platforms such as Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Adobe Commerce, CommerceTools, Shopify Plus, or SAP Commerce. Experience with B2B commerce, account structures, price lists, catalogs, promotions, customer groups, checkout complexity, and operational workflows. Experience supporting multi-region or global commerce rollouts with localization, currency, tax, language, payments, and regional operating differences. Experience with headless or composable commerce ecosystems, including front-end frameworks, CMS, search, personalization, and content operations. Experience with Azure-based integration patterns, API management, serverless orchestration, monitoring, and DevOps-enabled delivery. Critical Traits Strong point of view: Brings recommendations and the rationale behind them. Comfortable saying no: Stops weak designs, risky shortcuts, and decisions that create avoidable debt. Executive presence: Explains architecture choices in business terms and drives sponsor-level decisions. Operates in ambiguity: Moves the work forward without perfect information or full consensus. Accountability mindset: Owns architectural outcomes through implementation, not just design approval. Pragmatic judgment: Knows when to standardize, when to compromise, and when to escalate. Work Environment Our team members are our family, so we help our team members care for their families. The rewards of joining GES are extensive. We offer a comprehensive benefits package to all full-time employees. Here are some of the highlights: Competitive salaries 401K with company match Healthcare/vision/dental insurance Wellness benefits Career development program Employee assistance program Vacation time Community involvement opportunities Team activities And much more……
